20	## Service contract
21	
22	`ctx.trajectories.export({ sessions?, sink, rewardedOnly? })` folds each named session (or every persisted session when `sessions` is absent) through `ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect()` and writes `JSON.stringify(trajectory) + '\n'` to `sink.write()`; a session that cannot be read or folded is added to `skipped` with its reason and the export continues; `rewardedOnly: true` withholds trajectories whose reward outcome is not `1` and counts them as `filtered`. The sink is closed exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. The report carries `sessions`, `exported`, `rewarded`, `filtered`, and `skipped`. `jsonlFileSink(path)` is the shipped file sink; it truncates the file on first use.
23	
24	`foldTrajectory(meta, events)` is the pure projection behind the service and is exported for tests and offline tools. It is deterministic for the same inputs.
25	
26	## Record format `dsh-trajectory/1`
27	
28	| Field | Content |
29	|---|---|
30	| `id`, `source` | Session id; creation time, working directory, parent session, and the agent preset the log last selected |
31	| `config`, `system`, `tools` | Call configuration, rendered system prompt, and tool schemas of the last `request/header` |
32	| `messages` | Surface messages in model-visible order after compaction replacements: `user`, `assistant` (with `toolCalls` when requested), and `tool` (with `toolCallId`, `isError`) roles; each carries the `seq` of its source event, its `turn` and `step`, its content blocks verbatim (reasoning included), and the recorded source kind |
33	| `steps` | One entry per model call with the adapter-reported usage |
34	| `reward` | `outcome` `1` when a certificate covers the current standard revision, `0` when a standard exists without one, `null` otherwise; `basis` `certificate`, `uncertified-completion` (goal completed, no standard ever authored), or `none` (no goal); the goal snapshot, the covering certificate, and the directive and relaxation counts |
35	| `provenance` | Component ids in the component registry's scheme (`composition:<preset>`, `model-provider:<provider>`, `tool:<name>`), tool names in first-use order, and the certificate's isolation level |

40

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-verification
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Event-sourced executable completion standards for an agent session's goal. A validator authors the standard before implementation, may extend it, and may weaken it only through an evidenced relaxation; a certificate is recorded only by a fully passing run, and completion admission asks for exactly that certificate. The [verification-seams Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: verification
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
12	  config:
13	    maxChecks: 256
14	    maxTextChars: 16384
15	```
16	
17	`maxChecks` bounds one standard's active checks; `maxTextChars` bounds every recorded outcome, run instruction, evidence, root-cause, and detail text. Both must be positive safe integers.
18	
19	## Service contract
20	
21	`ctx.completionStandards` accepts only the exact live `Agent` instance registered under its id. `get()` returns a detached `StandardView`; mutations use a `StandardRef { id, revision }` compare-and-set fence and reject stale refs. At most one standard is current per session; `author()` creates a revision-one standard for a goal and rejects a second standard for the same goal, while a standard for a different goal supersedes the previous one. `extend()` appends checks and never rewrites existing ones; `relax()` removes exactly one check and records non-empty unsatisfiability evidence. `recordRun()` demands exactly one result per active check: a fully passing run commits a durable certificate in check order, and any failure returns the failing subset without a durable record. `issueDirective()` records the root-cause aggregation a consumer relays to the implementer. `assertCertified()` returns the certificate covering the exact current revision for one goal and otherwise throws, which makes it the admission read an orchestrator places before `ctx.goals.complete()`. When a goal service is composed, the service also registers the same admission as a deny-only `completionGuard()` on `ctx.goals`, so `GoalService.complete()` itself rejects an uncertified completion of a measured goal; unmeasured goals complete untouched.
22	
23	Every mutation appends one durable session event carrying complete post-mutation state: `verification/standard` (author, extend), `verification/relaxation`, `verification/certificate`, or `verification/directive`. Strict replay validates revisions, append-only check growth, relaxation shape, certificate coverage, and timestamp continuity, and any standard mutation invalidates the prior certificate. The session log is the only durable authority; a fresh service instance rebuilds its view from it.
24	
25	The separately published `./invariant` companion maintains an independent fold of each attached session. It rejects malformed verification changes before they enter the durable log, and rejects a `goal/change` completion for a goal that a current standard measures without a covering certificate.
26	
27	## Extension points
28	
29	Policy consumers call the service verbs and fold the four events from the session log. When a projection registry is composed, a `verification` session projection serves the same state to clients: the whole current standard with its certificate and directive count, `null` before authorship. A certificate is a replayable record of which checks passed with what evidence and under which isolation level (`none`, `process`, `host`), so evaluation and training-data pipelines can score sessions from the log alone: per-agent tallies of certificates earned, directives received, and relaxations recorded derive from the events without new instrumentation. Consumers use the `Agent` interface and session events rather than importing the agent loop.
30	
31	## Model Experience
32	
33	Indirectly, through the policy consumers that relay `verification/directive` text to the implementer and admit goal completion; every event this service appends is log-only and never enters model history.
34	
35	#### KV Cache effect
36	
37	No direct invalidation; a relaying consumer owns any request-prefix changes its messages cause.
38	
39	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
40	
41	- **Admission requires the goal service** — enforcement runs inside `GoalService.complete()` through the registered completion guard when both services are composed; an assembly without `ctx.goals` keeps only the service verbs and `assertCertified()` for its own callers, and the invariant companion still rejects an uncertified completion stream wherever it is installed.
42	- **No read barrier** — this package owns durable state only; denying implementer reads of standard artifacts is filesystem-policy work in a separate plugin, and until it exists the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log.
43	- **Directive delivery is consumer work** — directives are log-only records; without a consumer that relays them as plugin-sourced user messages, the implementer never sees them.
44	- **No run executor** — the validator agent executes checks with its own tools and reports results; this package records outcomes and never spawns processes.
45	- **Trusted in-process producers** — a plugin with direct `Session` access can append counterfeit verification data. Strict replay detects malformed or inconsistent records and fails at that record; this is integrity detection, not plugin isolation.
46

1 # Skills 2 3 English | [中文](skills.zh.md) 4 5 The [skill capability family](../../packages/skill) includes the Service Definition ([dsh-skill](../../packages/skill/skill), `ctx.skills`), the local Service Provider ([dsh-skill-filesystem](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem)), the optional packaged badge provider ([dsh-skill-badge](../../packages/skill/skill-badge)), and the Consumer ([dsh-tool-skill](../../packages/skill/tool-skill)). The registry merges provider catalogs across its host and per-scope layers; providers contribute local or packaged skills; the Consumer owns the initial and replacement catalogs plus the model-facing `skill` tool. Skills are optional instructions, not session events, so their vocabulary lives here rather than in [core.md](core.md). 6 7 Source: [`packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts), [`packages/skill/skill-filesystem/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem/src/index.ts), [`packages/skill/skill-badge/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/skill-badge/src/index.ts), and [`packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts). 8 9 ## Provider registry 10 11 `ctx.skills` combines local, embedded, remote, or other providers. Registration is synchronous; remote initialization and discovery belong in awaited `list()`. Provider objects, options, and candidates are borrowed readonly, while semantic fields are validated. 12 13 The registry is host+per-scope layered, the shape the [tools registry](tools.md) established over [dsh-scope](../../packages/core/scope): a registration files into the layer of its calling context's scope, so host rows and repository plugins land in the global layer while a plugin mounted by an agent preset's standing composition lands in that preset's layer, and provider names are unique per layer rather than process-wide. A read merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain — the nearest layer's entry wins a duplicate skill name outright, and the rank order below decides duplicates only within one layer. Discovery caches are keyed by the resolved scope chain, so re-parenting a scope (a blank-session recompose) is visible to the next read without a registry mutation. 14 15 Within one layer, duplicate names resolve by rank, provider order, then local order; summaries sort by name. A rejected `list()` is logged and omitted from an incomplete observation, while an explicit incomplete observation contributes usable candidates without making the result cacheable; malformed candidates fail fast. Each provider factory receives a registration-scoped control whose `invalidate()` clears completed catalogs only while that exact registration remains active and whose signal aborts on failed registration or disposal. An in-flight discovery retries once when its provider generation changes; a second change returns the latest candidates incomplete and uncached. Provider and runtime mutations emit the unfiltered `skills/change` invalidation event; it carries no diff, so consumers refetch `snapshot()` with their own lookup options. 16 17 An array returned by `SkillProvider.list()` is complete-discovery shorthand. `SkillProviderObservation` lets a provider expose candidates that remain directly loadable while reporting that the observation is not authoritative. 18 19 ```ts type-equiv 20 /** Provider candidates plus whether the current discovery is authoritative. */ 21 interface SkillProviderObservation { 22 /** Candidates available from the current provider discovery. */ 23 readonly candidates: readonly SkillCandidate[] 24 /** Whether discovery completed and these candidates may be cached. */ 25 readonly complete: boolean 26 } 27 ``` 28 29 ```ts type-equiv 30 /** Provider interface for one source of skills, such as local directories or a remote registry. */ 31 interface SkillProvider { 32 /** Unique provider name in the `ctx.skills` registry. */ 33 readonly name: string 34 /** 35 * List available skill candidates for the current lookup context. Provider 36 * plugins register synchronously during `apply()`; remote initialization, 37 * authentication, and discovery are awaited inside this method. Implementations 38 * should settle promptly when `options.signal` aborts. 39 * @param options - lookup options; `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills and `signal` cancels work. 40 * @returns provider candidates as a complete-array shorthand, or an explicit 41 * observation when usable candidates came from incomplete discovery. 42 */ 43 readonly list: (options: SkillLookupOptions) => Promise 44 /** 45 * Load a complete skill body for a previously listed candidate. 46 * @param candidate - the winning candidate originally returned by this provider. 47 * @param options - lookup options; `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills and `signal` cancels work. 48 * @returns the full skill body, or `undefined` if it is no longer loadable. 49 */ 50 readonly get: (candidate: SkillCandidate, options: SkillLookupOptions) => Promise 51 } 52 ``` 53 54 ```ts type-equiv 55 /** Registration-scoped lifecycle and invalidation capability borrowed by one provider. */ 56 interface SkillProviderControl { 57 /** Aborts if registration fails or when the exact provider registration is disposed. */ 58 readonly signal: AbortSignal 59 /** Invalidate completed catalogs and notify consumers only while the exact registration remains active. */ 60 readonly invalidate: () => void 61 } 62 ``` 63 64 ## Local discovery priority 65 66 The shipped local provider scans roots in rank order: 67 68 | Rank | Source | Root | 69 |---|---|---| 70 | 100 | `project-dsh` | `/.dsh/skills` | 71 | 200 | `project-agents` | `/.agents/skills` | 72 | 300 | `custom` | `Config.customSkillDirs` | 73 | 400 | `user-dsh` | `/skills` | 74 | 500 | `user-agents` | `/skills` | 75 | 600 | `bundled` | `Config.bundledSkillDir` when configured | 76 77 The project root is the nearest ancestor containing `.git`; without one, the current cwd is used. When `ctx.fs` is available, the git-root walk probes `.git` through the filesystem service so remote or sandboxed workspaces do not fall back to the host filesystem boundary. The user DSH root skips its `.system` child. The local provider does not synthesize built-in system skills; deployments supply packaged skills through configured bundled roots or dedicated providers. 78 79 `dsh-skill-badge` registers one immutable `bundled` candidate at `BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK` and exposes its packaged asset directory through `resourceBase`. The shipped CLI declares the plugin disabled, so enabling its composition row is an explicit opt-in. 80 81 Chokidar watches existing roots for direct bundle/flat-entry additions and removals plus direct skill-entry changes. A missing root is followed one absent path segment at a time from its nearest existing ancestor until Chokidar can attach. Resource files below a bundle are not catalog changes. Model-facing `write` and `edit` observations synchronously invalidate the provider when their target is catalog-relevant, while the host watcher covers IDE, Git, shell, and external-process mutations. Watcher failures make the current observation incomplete without hiding readable candidates from direct loads; project-scoped watchers use a configured bounded LRU. 82 83 ## Skill identity 84 85 Skill names are kebab-case (`^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`). The local provider accepts directory bundles (`/SKILL.md`) and flat Markdown files (`.md`). Nested recursive `**/SKILL.md` discovery is not supported. 86 87 ```ts type-equiv 88 /** Origin bucket for a skill contribution. The value is prompt-visible metadata, not precedence by itself. */ 89 type SkillSource = 'project-dsh' | 'project-agents' | 'runtime' | 'user-dsh' | 'user-agents' | 'custom' | 'bundled' | (string & {}) 90 ``` 91 92 ## Summaries, candidates, and complete definitions 93 94 `SkillSummary` is the registry's invocation-neutral summary shape. Consumers choose which entries and fields to render; the model session catalog uses only model-invocable `name` and `description`, never the body or absolute file path. `SkillInvocationPolicy` normalizes the two independent invocation controls into positive booleans, and every resolved summary, candidate, and definition carries it without turning arbitrary frontmatter into the domain model. 95 96 ```ts type-equiv 97 /** Invocation controls shared by skill discovery consumers. */ 98 interface SkillInvocationPolicy { 99 /** Whether model-facing catalogs and loaders include this skill. */ 100 readonly modelInvocable: boolean 101 /** Whether human-facing command catalogs and loaders include this skill. */ 102 readonly userInvocable: boolean 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 ```ts type-equiv 107 /** Invocation-neutral skill metadata returned by `ctx.skills.list()`. */ 108 interface SkillSummary { 109 /** Kebab-case identifier used to address the skill. */ 110 readonly name: string 111 /** Short routing description shown by discovery consumers. */ 112 readonly description: string 113 /** Optional extra routing guidance. */ 114 readonly whenToUse?: string 115 /** Resolved model and user invocation controls. */ 116 readonly invocation: SkillInvocationPolicy 117 /** Discovery source that produced this winning skill. */ 118 readonly source: SkillSource 119 /** Provider that owns this skill body. */ 120 readonly provider: string 121 /** Provider-specific base for relative resources. */ 122 readonly resourceBase?: SkillResourceBase 123 } 124 ``` 125 126 `ctx.skills.list()` preserves all four policy combinations. `isModelInvocable(skill)` and `isUserInvocable(skill)` read the corresponding required field. A model-only skill sets `{ modelInvocable: true, userInvocable: false }`, a user-only skill sets `{ modelInvocable: false, userInvocable: true }`, and setting both fields to `false` keeps the skill available only through trusted `ctx.skills.get()` callers. The local provider reads the exact kebab-case frontmatter keys `disable-model-invocation` and `user-invocable`, defaults omitted fields to `true`, and projects every parsed skill into this normalized policy. 127 128 `SkillCatalogSnapshot` distinguishes authoritative absence from transient provider failure or a catalog that kept changing during discovery. `skills` contains the sorted invocation-neutral summaries collected in that observation; `complete` is true only when every registered provider completed without a concurrent catalog revision. Incomplete snapshots are not cached, allowing each consumer to retain its last-good filtered catalog and retry. 129 130 ```ts type-equiv 131 /** One catalog observation plus whether discovery completed within a stable catalog revision. */ 132 interface SkillCatalogSnapshot { 133 /** Sorted invocation-neutral summaries collected in this observation. */ 134 readonly skills: SkillSummary[] 135 /** Whether every registered provider completed without a concurrent catalog revision. */ 136 readonly complete: boolean 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 `SkillCandidate` is the provider-to-registry shape. `locator` is opaque provider state; the registry only stores it and gives it back to the winning provider's `get()`. 141 142 ```ts type-equiv 143 /** Provider catalog entry used by the registry to merge and later load skills. */ 144 interface SkillCandidate extends SkillSummary { 145 /** Lower ranks win duplicate skill names before provider registration order is considered. */ 146 readonly rank: number 147 /** Opaque provider-owned handle passed back to `provider.get()`. */ 148 readonly locator: unknown 149 /** Absolute file path when the provider has one. */ 150 readonly path?: string 151 /** Parsed optional metadata object from provider-specific skill frontmatter. */ 152 readonly metadata?: Readonly> 153 } 154 ``` 155 156 `SkillDefinition` is the complete parsed result returned by `ctx.skills.get()` and used by the `skill` tool. `resourceBase` tells the tool how to render relative-resource guidance for local, URL, or provider-managed skills. 157 158 ```ts type-equiv 159 /** Optional provider-specific base used by loaded skill bodies to resolve relative resources. */ 160 type SkillResourceBase = 161 | { readonly kind: 'directory'; readonly path: string } 162 | { readonly kind: 'url'; readonly url: string } 163 | { readonly kind: 'opaque'; readonly description: string } 164 ``` 165 166 ```ts type-equiv 167 /** Complete parsed skill definition, including the body loaded by `ctx.skills.get()`. */ 168 interface SkillDefinition extends SkillSummary { 169 /** Markdown instruction body after any provider-specific metadata removal. */ 170 readonly content: string 171 /** Absolute file path when the skill came from disk. */ 172 readonly path?: string 173 /** Parsed optional metadata object from frontmatter. */ 174 readonly metadata?: Readonly> 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 Runtime skill inputs may omit invocation controls and the provider label. The registry resolves both defaults once, then uses the same complete definition shape and first-wins collection order as providers. The returned disposer removes the contribution and invalidates discovery caches. 179 180 ```ts type-equiv 181 /** Runtime skill contribution accepted by `ctx.skills.register()`. */ 182 type SkillRegistration = Omit & { 183 /** Invocation controls; omission permits both model and user surfaces. */ 184 readonly invocation?: SkillInvocationPolicy 185 /** Provider label; omission uses the registry-owned runtime provider. */ 186 readonly provider?: string 187 } 188 ``` 189 190 ## Lookup and configuration 191 192 Skill lookup is cwd-sensitive because providers may expose workspace-local skills, and its optional signal cancels provider work for the caller. Registry reads additionally take the viewing scope — consumers pass the calling agent, which is its own scope key — through `SkillViewOptions`; the registry consumes `scope` for layer selection, and providers read only their `SkillLookupOptions` contract from the same borrowed options object. Cancellation is checked before and after catalog selection, including cache hits, and races both discovery and full-definition loading. If no git root is found, the local provider treats the supplied cwd itself as the project root. 193 194 Full definitions are not cached by the registry. Each `get()` calls the winning provider with the selected candidate, so the local provider rereads the current body. A definition whose name no longer matches that candidate is rejected and invalidates the exact provider for rediscovery. 195 196 ```ts type-equiv 197 /** Caller context used for cwd-sensitive and abortable provider work. */ 198 interface SkillLookupOptions { 199 /** Workspace selector for the current lookup. */ 200 readonly cwd?: string | undefined 201 /** Abort discovery or loading work for the current caller. */ 202 readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined 203 } 204 ``` 205 206 ```ts type-equiv 207 /** 208 * Registry read options: provider lookup context plus the viewing scope. 209 * The registry consumes `scope` to select layers; providers receive the same 210 * borrowed options object and read only their {@link SkillLookupOptions} 211 * contract from it. 212 */ 213 interface SkillViewOptions extends SkillLookupOptions { 214 /** Viewing scope (the calling agent); omitted reads the global layer alone. */ 215 readonly scope?: ScopeKey | undefined 216 } 217 ``` 218 219 The registry owns only its discovery-cache bound. The local provider owns filesystem roots (`dshHome`, `agentsHome`, `customSkillDirs`, and optional `bundledSkillDir`/`DSH_BUNDLED_SKILL_DIR`) plus watcher enablement, polling, stability, symlink, and project-capacity controls. The consumer owns its catalog description bound. Exact defaults and validation are in the generated [config catalog](../config-catalog.md). 220 221 ```ts type-equiv 222 /** Skill registry configuration. */ 223 interface Config { 224 /** Maximum number of completed cwd/provider catalogs kept in memory. */ 225 readonly collectCacheMaxEntries?: number 226 } 227 ``` 228 229 ## Session catalog and tool contract 230 231 `dsh-tool-skill` injects the initial durable user-role `` at the first `agent/pre-step` of a live session that observes a non-empty complete view. The catalog contains sorted skill `name` and normalized, XML-escaped `description` only; it omits bodies, paths, sources, providers, and routing hints. Discovery forwards the step's abort signal through `SkillLookupOptions`. `catalogDescriptionMaxLength` is the consumer config for the description bound, with default `500` and integer minimum `3`. 232 233 Before each later model step, the consumer applies exact tool visibility and digests the exact rendered entries between the `` tags from a complete snapshot. It derives the comparison baseline from the same entries in the newest recognizable visible catalog message sourced by the plugin. A changed digest appends a durable full replacement through `agent.inject()`; deleting every skill appends an explicit empty replacement. Incomplete snapshots preserve the last-good model view. If compaction hides every historical catalog message, the next complete snapshot re-establishes the current catalog; an empty view with no prior catalog emits nothing. These catalog messages are session history, not World State. 234 235 The model-facing `skill({ name })` tool validates the kebab-case name, finds the summary in the invocation-neutral catalog, rejects it before loading unless `isModelInvocable` permits access, then rereads the complete definition for the calling agent cwd and rechecks the policy before returning content. It reports an unresolved skill as unknown or no longer available and returns a tool result containing ``, ``, and ``. `resourceBase` resolves explicitly referenced scripts, references, and assets only as needed; the loaded result does not enumerate a skill directory. Body-only edits therefore change later tool calls without producing catalog messages or rewriting earlier tool results. 236 237 238 239 240 241 ## Cordis API 242 243 Generated from source by `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts` (verified fresh by `pnpm run verify-cordis-catalog` in doc-sync; regenerate with `pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog`) — this section is byte-identical in both language sides of the page. Signature blocks use a `ts cordis-catalog` fence and keep the original source JSDoc; dispatch modes are defined in the [primer](../cordis-primer.md#dispatch-modes), and the framework-inherited `ctx` API lives in [cordis-api/inherited.md](../cordis-api/inherited.md). 244 245 246 247 ### `ctx.skills` — `SkillRegistry` 248 249 Layered registry of skill providers, the host+per-scope shape the tools registry established. A registration files into the layer of its calling context's scope (scopeOf): host rows and repository plugins land in the global layer, while a plugin mounted by an agent preset's standing composition lands in that preset's layer. A read merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain — the nearest layer's entry wins a duplicate name outright, and the rank order decides duplicates only within one layer. It exposes sorted invocation-neutral summaries and loads full skill bodies on demand. 250 251 ```ts cordis-catalog 252 /** 253 * Register a borrowed same-process provider synchronously during plugin 254 * apply, into the calling context's layer: a scoped context (an agent 255 * preset's standing mount) registers for that scope alone, an unscoped 256 * context registers globally. Duplicate names within one layer and reserved 257 * names throw; remote initialization belongs in `list()`. Fiber disposal 258 * unregisters the provider and invalidates catalog caches. 259 * @param create - synchronous factory receiving this registration's lifecycle and invalidation control. 260 * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer that unregisters this provider; 261 * composite effects may yield it directly to preserve teardown ordering. 262 */ 263 registerProvider(create: (control: SkillProviderControl) => SkillProvider): () => void 264 265 /** 266 * Register a borrowed readonly runtime skill into the calling context's 267 * layer. Project entries outrank runtime entries, which outrank user 268 * entries, within one layer. Same-name runtime entries in one layer are 269 * first-wins; a duplicate logs a warning and receives a no-op disposer so 270 * it cannot remove the winner. 271 * @param skill - the skill definition input; omitted invocation and provider fields receive defaults. 272 * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer, preserving composite teardown order and invalidating caches. 273 */ 274 register(skill: SkillRegistration): () => void 275 276 /** 277 * List invocation-neutral skill summaries for a workspace. Consumers apply 278 * model or user invocation policy at their operational boundary. Lookup 279 * options and provider candidates are readonly same-process values borrowed 280 * throughout discovery. 281 * @param options - view options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers, `cwd` selects project roots, and `signal` cancels discovery. 282 * @returns all sorted winning summaries. 283 */ 284 async list(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise 285 286 /** 287 * Observe the current invocation-neutral catalog and whether discovery completed within a stable revision. 288 * Incomplete observations are never cached, allowing consumers to retain last-good state and 289 * retry on their next request boundary. 290 * @param options - view options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers, `cwd` selects project roots, and `signal` cancels discovery. 291 * @returns sorted summaries plus discovery-completeness state. 292 */ 293 async snapshot(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise 294 295 /** 296 * Load and validate the winning candidate, passing its opaque discovery locator back to the 297 * provider. Cancellation is rechecked after selection, including cache hits, and raced against 298 * loading so an uncooperative provider cannot hang the caller. 299 * @param name - kebab-case skill name. 300 * @param options - view options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers, 301 * `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills, and `signal` cancels work. 302 * @returns the full skill, including body content, or `undefined`. 303 */ 304 async get(name: string, options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise 305 ``` 306 307 Source: [`packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts:357`](../../packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts) 308 309 310 311 ### `skills/*` events 312 313 314 315 #### `skills/change` — emit 316 317 A skill provider, runtime contribution, or provider-backed catalog may have changed. This is an unfiltered invalidation notification; consumers refetch the catalog for their own lookup options.
